summary_en: SERAKU expanded its share buyback authorization from 500,000 shares (3.77% of issued shares excluding treasury stock) to 1,000,000 shares (7.55%) and the acquisition budget from 500 million yen to 1 billion yen. The acquisition period remains July 28, 2026 through June 30, 2027, using ToSTNeT-3 and market purchases on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
title_en: Notice Regarding Partial Amendment to Share Buyback Matters (Expansion of Acquisition Framework)
translation_en_brief:
On October 29, 2026, SERAKU's board of directors approved an expansion of its share buyback authorization. The company increased the maximum number of shares to acquire from 500,000 shares to 1,000,000 shares, representing 7.55% of issued shares excluding treasury stock (as of June 30, 2026). The acquisition budget was simultaneously raised from 500 million yen to 1 billion yen. The acquisition period extends from July 28, 2026 through June 30, 2027. The company will utilize ToSTNeT-3 (off-hours trading) and market purchases on the Tokyo Stock Exchange as acquisition methods.

The board cited three principal reasons for the framework expansion: enabling flexible capital policy execution in response to changing business conditions, providing shares for use in M&A transactions and employee incentive plans, and advancing shareholder returns. The acquisition by ToSTNeT-3 is intended to occur at the previous trading day's closing price. Two controlling shareholders—representative director Tatsumi Miyazaki and executive director Hiromi Miyazaki—are expected to participate as sellers in the ToSTNeT-3 component, triggering a related-party transaction classification. 

To protect minority shareholders, the company adopted safeguard measures. Only three directors (including two independent outside directors) participated in the board deliberation and resolution, excluding the two related parties. The company obtained an independent opinion from two committee members confirming that the transaction does not disadvantage minority shareholders and includes adequate fairness safeguards and conflict-of-interest avoidance measures.
